children: HCL Technologies' strong Q2 earnings, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) revenue and robust deal wins have strengthened the investment case for the IT stock, but concerns over valuations and the sustainability of a demand recovery could limit its upside. Brokerages remain divided on HCLTech's prospects after the company raised the lower end of its FY27 revenue growth guidance, with price targets suggesting potential returns ranging from an 11 percent decline to a 9 percent gain from Monday's closing price.

HCLTech shares closed at Rs 1,223 on Monday, up 0.52 percent ahead of the earnings announcement. The stock has declined 25.2 percent so far in 2026, compared with a 14.5 percent fall in the Nifty 50. The company's market capitalisation stands at Rs 3.32 lakh crore.

, implying an upside of nearly 9 percent from Monday's closing price. The brokerage highlighted strong performance in the services business, continued growth in AI revenue and steady progress on the company's five-pillar AI strategy.

Nomura expects operating margins to normalise over FY27 and FY28 and has raised its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for the two financial years by around 2-3 percent. It also noted that the midpoint of HCLTech's FY27 revenue growth guidance remains unchanged.

The brokerage said that revenue was broadly in line with expectations, while EBIT and EPS exceeded consensus estimates by 4 percent and 6 percent, respectively. CLSA highlighted the company's strong order book, growing advanced AI revenue and large deal wins, which could support market share gains.
However, it expects FY27 constant-currency revenue growth of 3 percent, towards the lower end of the company's revised guidance. The brokerage raised its FY27 EPS estimate by 2 percent.
HCLTech Q2 results: Profit rises 21% YoY, AI revenue jumps 78%

HCLTech reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 5,132 crore for the September quarter, up 21.2 percent year-on-year and 11 percent sequentially. Revenue from operations rose 11.5 percent year-on-year to Rs 35,620 crore, while operating margin expanded 131 basis points sequentially and 71 basis points annually to 18.2 percent.

Advanced AI revenue surged 78 percent year-on-year and 28.4 percent sequentially to $219 million, underscoring the growing contribution of AI-led services. The company also reported net new deal wins worth $3.24 billion, including a $1.14 billion mega AI deal from Mercedes-Benz.

HCLTech revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 2.5-4 percent from 1-4 percent earlier, raising the lower end while keeping the midpoint unchanged. Its operating margin guidance was retained at 17.5-18.5 percent. The company also announced a Global Premier Partnership with Anthropic to accelerate enterprise adoption of agentic AI, focusing on safety, cybersecurity and governance.
